audit.whatIsWrong: The page carries diff 'FAV' alongside diffRating '8/10', tone '#ff5d6c' (red), and prose reading 'Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10, Swain carry threat 8.5/10' in two places. The Emerald+ win rate is 62.72% over 1191 games — the strongest matchup in this slice. carryRating '8.5/10' also contradicts breakdown.carry, which says 7/10 in the same file.
audit.why: A player opening the highest-win-rate matchup on the page and being told it is an 8/10 hard lane will play it scared and concede a lane he wins outright. The FAV label and the win rate agree with each other; the rating, the colour and the prose are the outliers.
audit.corrected: diffRating 3.5/10, tone green, carryRating aligned to the 7/10 the page already states, and both difficulty strings rewritten as favoured.

audit.whatIsWrong: One row off: the packet has First item as Skill, both layers had Garen. The page's own whys[5] says 'First item stays even as his sustain matches your pressure' — which is Skill, not Garen.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock's healing and permanent max-health growth catch up to Garen's pressure around the first completed item, which is exactly what the existing why describes.
audit.corrected: First item set to Skill in both layers with the rating dropped to 5/10; the rest of the chart already matched the packet and was left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike was written around 'Rylai's/Liandry's Swain's DPS and self-heal climb' with no mention of the two flagged missing interactions, both of which are itemization facts that land exactly at that spike.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently increases his maximum health, so Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade, and his percent-health chip means raw armour or MR is the wrong purchase. That is what actually changes at first item.
audit.corrected: First-item spike rewritten around Grievous Wounds and the resistances trap.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5] listed Demonic Ascension's cooldown as an em dash — no number at all. It is 120s flat at every rank, and Riot's text adds that the form 'is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions'. Nevermove was described only as an 'E root' and a 'linear root claw'; Riot's text is specific: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN, and the page never said so. The page also twice told the player to silence Swain's 'ult channel'.
audit.why: Which half of Nevermove roots is the whole counterplay. A player told to 'dodge his E' sidesteps the outgoing wave, stands still, and gets rooted by the return — then pulled. Stating that it roots coming back turns a coinflip into a positioning rule. Demonic Ascension's duration being drain-dependent rather than fixed is also actionable: walking out of the 650 range ends it, which is different advice from waiting out a timer.
audit.corrected: Nevermove's return-wave root promoted to tldr, focus, mistakes, spikes and wants; Demonic Ascension given its real 120s cooldown and drain-dependent duration.

audit.whatIsWrong: All-in and jungle windows keyed to Demonic Ascension, a 120s ultimate, rather than to the lockdown that actually stops a Garen run-down.
audit.why: Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 is the spell that catches him a Garen. If it is down, Swain has no way to stop a Q-move-speed approach at all.
audit.corrected: All-in window re-keyed to Nevermove's 12s rank-1 cooldown.
